samples.summary: `defaultKeys` pinning only covers cells that exist in the store, so empty cells in the selection lose an inherited `nf` to the range patch
samples.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` iterates `await this.store.getGrid(range)` (sheet.ts:3828) and can therefore only pin formats for cells that already have a store entry. `changeDecimals` then calls `setRangeStyle({dp, nf:'number'}, {defaultKeys:['nf']})` (sheet.ts:4359), and for a cell selection the patch is appended over the *whole range* via `addRangeStylePatch` — the range layer sits above sheet/column/row in `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:917). Concretely: column A has a column style `{nf:'percent'}` and only A1 holds a value; selecting A1:A5 and pressing Decrease writes a patch `{dp:0, nf:'number'}` over A1:A5. A1 keeps percent (it is pinned), but A2..A5 — which exist only as inherited style — are now `nf:'number'`, so typing 0.5 into A3 afterwards renders `0.50` instead of `50%`. The doc comment claims a neighbour "rendering through its own percent/currency/date format keeps it", which is only true for populated cells.

samples.summary: The unset deletes a user-chosen `nf:'number'` together with `dp` whenever rendering happens to coincide (values < 1000)
samples.evidence: `const values = nf === 'number' ? { dp, nf } : { dp };` (sheet.ts:4344-4345) hands both keys to `unsetRangeStyleValues`, guarded only by `unsetKeepsRendering`, which compares the *current* values (sheet.ts:4433-4436). For a cell the user explicitly formatted as Number holding `12`, stepping down to `dp:1` and pressing Decrease once more gives target 0 === valueDp 0, and `formatValue('12', undefined, undefined) === formatValue('12','number',0) === '12'`, so the unset fires and `nf:'number'` is deleted. Nothing on screen moves at that instant, but the user's format is gone: entering `1234` afterwards renders `1234` instead of `1,234`. The tests only step down to dp 2 (`test/sheet/decimals.test.ts` "should keep a number format the user chose"), so this path is unasserted. `docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-lessons.md:45` documents this as an accepted deviation, which is why confidence on it being *intended* is mixed — but it is still silent loss of user formatting.

samples.summary: `nf:'number'` is only added when the ACTIVE cell renders raw, so plain neighbours in a mixed selection get a `dp` that never renders
samples.evidence: `if (!nf || nf === 'plain') { patch.nf = 'number'; ... }` (sheet.ts:4352-4360) keys the decision off the active cell alone. If the active cell already has `nf:'number'`/`'percent'`, the else branch runs `setRangeStyle({dp: target})` with no `nf`, so a plain-format neighbour in the same selection stores a `dp` that `formatValue` ignores (`if (!format || format === 'plain') return value;`, format.ts:205). Pressing Increase/Decrease then visibly changes some cells of the selection and silently does nothing for others.

samples.summary: A single Decrease press collapses a neighbour's decimals from N to 0 rather than stepping by one
samples.evidence: When the active cell is already at zero decimals, `clamped = stepped < 0; const target = clamped ? 0 : stepped;` (sheet.ts:4328-4329) writes `dp: 0` for the whole selection. With A1 = `12` (0 decimals) and B1 = `1.2345`, one Decrease sets B1 to 0 decimals instead of 3 — the step is not "by one" for any cell whose precision differs from the active cell's. The new test at test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:154 pins this behaviour, so it is deliberate, but it is a boundary/step-size inconsistency worth naming.

samples.summary: `currencyDecimals` builds a fresh `Intl.NumberFormat` per cell inside the new whole-selection scans
samples.evidence: `renderedDecimals` calls `currencyDecimals` (format.ts:149-161), which constructs `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)` with no memoisation, and `selectionRendersAt` calls `renderedDecimals` for every populated cell in every selected range (sheet.ts:4386). `unsetKeepsRendering` likewise calls `formatValue` twice per cell (sheet.ts:4434-4435). A Ctrl+A Decrease on a sheet of dp-less currency cells therefore constructs one `Intl.NumberFormat` per cell synchronously on a button press — `Intl` constructor cost is the classic source of multi-second jank in exactly this shape.

samples.summary: `unsetRangeStyleValues` replaces the whole `rangeStyles` array on a routine button press, which can clobber a concurrent peer's patch
samples.evidence: `this.rangeStyles = nextPatches; await this.store.setRangeStyles(this.rangeStyles);` (sheet.ts:4627-4628). In the Yorkie store `setRangeStyles` assigns the array wholesale (`root.sheets[tabId].rangeStyles = normalized.map(...)`, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:835/848), unlike `addRangeStyle` which pushes. Any patch a collaborator appended since this client's last load is dropped. The pattern pre-exists in `addRangeStylePatch`'s compaction path, but this change makes it fire on the ordinary Decrease round trip.

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` mis-reads exponent and non-numeric values, feeding a wrong `valueDp`/`dp` into the step arithmetic
samples.evidence: `decimalsInValue` counts every character after the first '.' (format.ts:137-138). `'1.5e-7'` reports 4, `'abc.def'` reports 3, and a value with 25 stored decimals reports 25 — which `changeDecimals` then clamps to 20, so an *Increase* press on such a plain cell reduces the digits shown from 25 to 20 (`Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)`, sheet.ts:4317), and `target === valueDp` can never hold again so the round trip never restores inheritance. The old code had the same dot-scan, but it now feeds the new `valueDp`/`explicitDp` reversibility logic.

samples.summary: `renderedDecimals` reports a date-formatted cell's raw precision, so a Decrease that should be a no-op writes a style
samples.evidence: `if (!nf || nf === 'plain' || nf === 'date') return decimalsInValue(value);` (format.ts:181-183). A date cell holding a serial value such as `'45000.5'` displays a date string with no decimals, but `renderedDecimals` reports 1, so `selectionRendersAt(0)` returns false (sheet.ts:4386) and `changeDecimals` writes `{dp: 0}` (plus `nf:'number'` when the active cell is plain) over a selection that had nothing to drop.

finding.summary: `defaultKeys` pinning only covers cells that exist in the store, so empty cells in the selection lose an inherited `nf` to the range patch
finding.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` iterates `await this.store.getGrid(range)` (sheet.ts:3828) and can therefore only pin formats for cells that already have a store entry. `changeDecimals` then calls `setRangeStyle({dp, nf:'number'}, {defaultKeys:['nf']})` (sheet.ts:4359), and for a cell selection the patch is appended over the *whole range* via `addRangeStylePatch` — the range layer sits above sheet/column/row in `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:917). Concretely: column A has a column style `{nf:'percent'}` and only A1 holds a value; selecting A1:A5 and pressing Decrease writes a patch `{dp:0, nf:'number'}` over A1:A5. A1 keeps percent (it is pinned), but A2..A5 — which exist only as inherited style — are now `nf:'number'`, so typing 0.5 into A3 afterwards renders `0.50` instead of `50%`. The doc comment claims a neighbour "rendering through its own percent/currency/date format keeps it", which is only true for populated cells.

verdict.reason: The described mechanism is real. `collectStyleValuesToPin` (sheet.ts:3818-3850) pins only cells returned by `store.getGrid(range)` (sheet.ts:3828), and both store implementations emit only existing entries (memory.ts:145-157, readonly.ts:105-115), so cells that exist solely as inherited style are never pinned. Meanwhile `setRangeStyle` appends the patch over the entire range via `addRangeStylePatch` (sheet.ts:3800, 1873-1976), which is not population-limited (unlike `applyStylePatchToExistingCells`, sheet.ts:1978-2001), and the range layer outranks sheet/column/row in `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:917). `changeDecimals` uses this path with `defaultKeys:['nf']` (sheet.ts:4359), so empty cells inside the selection that inherit `nf:'percent'/'currency'/'date'` from a column/row/sheet style are silently converted to `nf:'number'`, breaking the invariant documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:266-268 and only covered for populated cells by the test at test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:596-612. The reviewer's exact single-column repro is imprecise (a whole-column percent style would also make the active cell percent, skipping the `nf:'number'` branch at sheet.ts:4352-4359), but a mixed-column selection (A1 plain + column B percent with only B1 populated, selecting A1:B5) reproduces it: B1 keeps percent, B2..B5 render later-typed values as numbers. No guard makes it unreachable, so it stands as a correctness/broken-invariant defect.

finding.summary: The unset deletes a user-chosen `nf:'number'` together with `dp` whenever rendering happens to coincide (values < 1000)
finding.evidence: `const values = nf === 'number' ? { dp, nf } : { dp };` (sheet.ts:4344-4345) hands both keys to `unsetRangeStyleValues`, guarded only by `unsetKeepsRendering`, which compares the *current* values (sheet.ts:4433-4436). For a cell the user explicitly formatted as Number holding `12`, stepping down to `dp:1` and pressing Decrease once more gives target 0 === valueDp 0, and `formatValue('12', undefined, undefined) === formatValue('12','number',0) === '12'`, so the unset fires and `nf:'number'` is deleted. Nothing on screen moves at that instant, but the user's format is gone: entering `1234` afterwards renders `1234` instead of `1,234`. The tests only step down to dp 2 (`test/sheet/decimals.test.ts` "should keep a number format the user chose"), so this path is unasserted. `docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-lessons.md:45` documents this as an accepted deviation, which is why confidence on it being *intended* is mixed — but it is still silent loss of user formatting.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as quoted and the behavioral trace checks out: `sheet.ts:4344-4345` passes `{dp, nf}` to `unsetRangeStyleValues`, gated only by `unsetKeepsRendering` (`sheet.ts:4433-4436`), and since `formatValue('12', undefined, undefined) === formatValue('12','number',0) === '12'` (`format.ts:205-207`, `218-225`), a user-chosen `nf:'number'` on a small value is dropped when dp is stepped to valueDp. However, this is not a logic/runtime defect: it is the change's explicitly specified and accepted behavior. The task doc's "Known deviations" (`docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:91-99`) and the shipped design doc (`docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:280-284`) both state that an unattributable `nf:'number'` is deliberately dropped when the step lands on the value's own precision, note the divergence from Google Sheets, and bound it to cases where nothing on screen changes; the implementation matches that spec (todo lines 63-70). The disagreement is with a deliberate product/scope tradeoff about unattributable formatting, not a wrong condition, boundary error, missing guard, dropped await, or unintended overwrite, so it falls outside the Correctness lane (design/product owns it; the internal doc inconsistency at sheet-style.md:226-229 vs :280-284 belongs to the docs lens).

finding.summary: Increase/Decrease Decimals becomes a visual no-op for cells whose effective format is explicitly `nf: 'plain'` — the new pinning writes `'plain'` back over the `'number'` the step needs
finding.evidence: `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4352-4359) sets `patch.nf = 'number'` and passes `{ defaultKeys: ['nf'] }` when the active cell's `nf` is falsy **or** `'plain'`. In the cell path, `collectStyleValuesToPin` (sheet.ts:3836-3844) pins any effective value that differs from the patch: for a cell whose effective `nf` is the explicit string `'plain'`, `value ('plain') !== patch.nf ('number')`, so `keep = { nf: 'plain' }` is written back at cell level *after* the patch lands (sheet.ts:3802-3804). The stepped `dp` is therefore stored but never rendered — `formatValue` returns the raw value for `nf === 'plain'` (format.ts:205-207) — and the cell is permanently pinned to `plain` at cell level. Explicit `nf:'plain'` is common: xlsx import emits it (`packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:254` for numFmtId 49 and :294 for `@`), the toolbar 'Plain' item applies it (`packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:417/843` → `applyStyle({nf:'plain'})`), and `DefaultResetStylePatch` contains `nf:'plain'` (sheet.ts:163). The same hole exists on the column/row/all paths via `withoutSetDefaults` (sheet.ts:3745/3762/3776), which drops `nf` whenever the layer already holds one — including `'plain'`. Every new test in `decimals.test.ts` uses `nf: undefined`, so this case is untested.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. changeDecimals (sheet.ts:4352-4359) treats effective nf === 'plain' the same as absent nf: it sets patch.nf = 'number' but marks nf as a *default* via { defaultKeys: ['nf'] }. In the cell path, collectStyleValuesToPin (sheet.ts:3836-3844) keeps any effective value differing from the patch, so effective nf 'plain' yields keep = { nf: 'plain' }, and that pin is written back AFTER the patch lands (sheet.ts:3800-3804), overwriting the 'number' the step requires. formatValue returns the raw value for 'plain' (format.ts:205-207), so the stepped dp is stored but never rendered — Increase/Decrease Decimals silently does nothing for such cells, and inherited 'plain' additionally becomes permanently pinned at cell level. The same hole exists on the column/row/all paths, where withoutSetDefaults (sheet.ts:171-191) deletes nf whenever the layer already holds one, including 'plain' (call sites sheet.ts:3745, 3762, 3776). Explicit nf:'plain' is reachable: xlsx import emits it (xlsx-styles.ts:254, :294), DefaultResetStylePatch contains it (sheet.ts:163, style-mutation.ts:31). No guard prevents this: the only early return (sheet.ts:4318-4324) applies solely to a decrease with no explicit dp when the whole selection already renders at 0 decimals, so an increase, or a plain value like '12.345', reaches the write. decimals.test.ts has no nf:'plain' coverage. Real logic bug breaking a core user flow — in the correctness lane, major.

mergedFrom.summary: `withoutSetDefaults` compares the patch only against the same layer, not the effective style, so column/row steps still override formats inherited from lower layers

finding.summary: Pinning materializes inherited column/row/sheet formats onto individual cells, permanently breaking style inheritance for those cells
finding.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` resolves the *effective* style (sheet.ts:3836) and then `setRangeStyle` writes those values onto the cell itself (`await this.setStyle(parseRef(sref), keep)`, sheet.ts:3803). A cell that merely *inherited* `nf: 'percent'` from a column/row/sheet layer now carries an explicit cell-level `nf: 'percent'`. After a single Increase Decimals over a wide selection, changing the column's number format no longer affects those cells (cell level wins in `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:917), and undo of the decimal step does not necessarily unwind the pinned cell writes. The test at decimals.test.ts:600-616 asserts only that the pinned render is right, not that inheritance survives.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `collectStyleValuesToPin` resolves the effective style including sheet/column/row/range layers (sheet.ts:3836) and `setRangeStyle` writes those values back onto the cells via `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3802-3804), which merges into `cell.s` and persists it (sheet.ts:3705-3721). This is reachable from a normal user action: `changeDecimals` calls `setRangeStyle(patch, { defaultKeys: ['nf'] })` when the active cell format is plain (sheet.ts:4351-4360). Since cell-level style wins in `resolveEffectiveStyle` (sheet.ts:907+), a cell that only inherited `nf: 'percent'` from a column/row/sheet layer now carries it explicitly and stops following later changes to that layer — a lossy/incorrect state update in the correctness lane. The test at decimals.test.ts:596-612 asserts only the rendered string, not that inheritance survives, so nothing guards this. I could only partially rebut the supporting undo claim (all writes share one `beginBatch`/`endBatch`, sheet.ts:3737/3807, documented as a single undo step in store.ts:275-284 and implemented as one `doc.update` in yorkie-store.ts:1158-1163), which does not neutralize the core finding. The design doc calls the pinning intentional (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:266-268), but intentional does not make the inheritance loss unreal, and that is not a named refutation ground I can apply with high confidence.
